title: C Memory
description: Can write C that owns pointers and heap so allocated memory is freed — and can choose a static budget, pool or ring buffer when malloc is the wrong tool.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can write C that allocates and frees heap memory, inspect stack versus heap in a debugger, and name whether a given argument is passed by pointer or by value — under written guidance.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can implement a dynamic list or hash table in C that frees every allocation, write a note that names stack, heap and common pointer errors, and show a captured debugger session that inspects a pointer and the bytes it addresses.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently ship a host-side C component with a written byte budget or fixed-size pool, a gate that rejects malloc, and a captured size or linker-map excerpt proving .data + .bss stay inside that budget.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can diagnose a leak, double-free, overflow or alignment fault that a return value alone would hide, cite the layout or overflow/OOM policy that explains it, and produce a note another engineer can follow to reproduce the fault without opening a debugger first.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's C memory work, name an unchecked malloc, missing free, or untested overflow/OOM path, and teach when a static buffer, pool or ring buffer is the right tool on an unfamiliar constrained target.
